title: Validated numerical linear algebra
objective: Implement the validated dense binary64 numerical linear algebra reference slice with independent residual and minimum-norm validation, bounded execution, and representative correctness and performance evidence

oracles: Deterministic NumPy/SciPy differential campaign, fixed fixtures, closed-form metamorphic identities, and independent compensated residual and row-space checks

handoff.summary: Implemented and audited the source-portable dense binary64 linear algebra slice: scale-safe norms, Jacobi diagnostics, and Householder QR; structured LU/QR/Cholesky and dimension failures; exact elapsed/cancellation guard plumbing; JSON-safe determinant overflow; correct strictly-positive Cholesky pivots; transpose-provenance minimum-norm solves with an independent row-space validator; and executable CPython/Sage.js, NumPy/SciPy, metamorphic, and benchmark evidence.
risks: Only Linux x64 CPython and Sage.js have a recorded runtime receipt; browser, Linux arm64, macOS arm64, and Windows x64 remain explicit target work.

The lane intentionally leaves shared exports, diagnostic/status registries other than its consumption of maximum_elapsed_time, package graphs, Pyright registration, and test-script discovery to integration.
This is an O(m*n*min(m,n)) ordinary-Python reference implementation, not an accelerated large-problem backend.
next_steps: Integration should apply docs/numerical-computing/linear-algebra/integration-requests.md, including shared exports and the remaining domain diagnostic/status identities.
Qualify the identical corpus on browser and the three pending native host classes before adding those platforms to validated_platforms.
Use the reference slice as the differential fallback for later accelerated, sparse, and spectral work.
